item.title: Occupied West Bank: Settler siege of Palestinians marks a new low: OHCHR
item.description: In the occupied West Bank, the UN human rights office, OHCHR, appealed on Thursday to Israeli authorities to help Palestinian families trapped in their homes by settlers for days, amid an intensifying campaign to seize their land.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Escalating attacks threaten peace in Yemen
item.description: As tensions triggered by the US-Iran war continue to ripple across the Middle East, the Security Council holds an open debate Thursday on Yemen, where escalating deadly military clashes are worsening an already fragile humanitarian situation amid fears that recent Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia and commercial vessels could threaten the 2022 truce between the Yemeni militia and the government. UN News app users can follow our live coverage here.

item.title: Ukraine: Civilian casualties hit highest level since March 2022
item.description: Civilian casualties in Ukraine reached their highest monthly level in July, with more people killed and injured than at any time since March 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in the country, HRMMU, said in an update on Thursday.

item.title: Türkiye’s changes to child detention ‘raise serious human rights concerns’
item.description: UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Thursday condemned an amendment adopted by Türkiye’s parliament that would allow judges to give life sentences to child offenders convicted of serious crimes.

item.title: World News in Brief: Afghanistan education, Myanmar flooding, Syria recovery, homecare workers in New York
item.description: Five years since the Taliban seized power in Kabul, life for some Afghans has improved while many others suffer growing hardship.

item.title: Gaza: Destruction of buildings rises by nearly 10 per cent since ceasefire
item.description: New satellite assessments show the destruction of buildings in Gaza has climbed by nearly 10 per cent since October’s faltering ceasefire between Hamas and Israeli forces aim to end the two-year war, which reduced cities to rubble and displaced more than one million people, UN agencies said on Thursday.

item.title: Ebola tracing improves in DR Congo – but the virus is still winning the race
item.description: Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are tracking a growing share of people exposed to Ebola, but the epidemic in the country's restive east continues to outpace their ability to find and isolate the sick, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

item.title: African Rights Advocates Coordinate Response to Family Law Backlash
item.description: Campaigners say anti-rights movements are increasingly using family law to challenge women's rights to inheritance, property, divorce and child custody.

item.title: Why Dhaka Floods Every Monsoon
item.description: Dhaka’s recent and recurrent flooding is often treated as a natural disaster, but rain is only the trigger. The deeper causes are political, planning and ecological failure: wetland loss, canal encroachment, unplanned growth, weak enforcement, fragmented institutions and short-term engineering fixes. item.title: Rising Trade Values Mask the True Cost of Global Supply Chain Disruptions
item.description: Global goods trade reached approximately USD 13.7 trillion in the first half of 2026, up 12.5 percent from the same period in 2025, while services grew 10.5 percent, together adding USD 2 trillion to global trade.
